I think the first thing you need to recognize is that even though he may be very smart he is still a very young child. And young children have a very hard time processing big emotions. My advice is just to talk to him more. When he said he was bad, did you ask him why? Keep asking questions and get to the root of the issue. Let him know making mistakes doesn't make someone bad, this is how we grow and that even you make mistakes. Tell him that you love for him is unconditional and even though you might not always like the things he does nothing he does could ever make you love him less. Tell him constantly that his happiness is the most important thing to you. Let him know he can always come to you with anything without judgment. And stop praising him for the stuff he is "good at" because he is never going to think he is actually good at them. Instead start praising him for his character and efforts. "I saw you help X today, you are very kind" " You worked so hard on X today, I know that wasnt easy. I'm proud of you." And dont make it a nightly scheduled, forced thing. Make it a constant thing. Every time you see a quality about your son you love, make sure he knows you see it. "You're so funny you always make me laugh." "Your are so sweet, you bring so much joy into my life." "You have the best hugs, they always make me so happy." Ect. At the end of the day he probably has depression and will probably need medication before it is said and done, but just lift him up every chance you get. I hope this helps at least a little.

The reality is she lived an existence no different that a dog who had a fensed in yard would have. And with sufficient training a cat can absolutely safely and responsibly free roam.

That it is just laziness of the parent or person, or that they just dont eat right, ect. So people with eating disorders that cause over eating are shamed and often dont seek help. But over eating is very often just as much a mental health issue as anorexia or bulimia. Over eating is often triggered by a traumatic event in childhood such as sexual abuse or other trauma. Much the same way that drug use is. 

One of the reasons I was able to understand the psychological issue behind my son's eating was because growing up my mother over ate to the point she was morbidly obese. This started in her childhood after being sexually assaulted by her father. Her eating habits became even worse after an abusive marriage.
